summary: Implemented src/platform/podman.ts with shell-free run/stop/remove/inspect/logs and volume create/list/remove, plus 38 recording-runner tests. Typecheck, lint, focused tests, the full 463-test suite, and the production build all pass.

decisions: Every Podman call uses an argument array and a finite timeout; run defaults to 600s, stop/remove/volume to 60s, inspect to 15s, and logs to 1h.
run emits exactly one --restart=always, one --publish, one --env PORT=<containerPort>, three io.easy-host labels, and one --volume easy-host-<app>-<volume>:<path> per declared mount.

The merged environment is passed as --env KEY=VALUE pairs in deterministic key order; PORT always overrides any app-supplied value. Diagnostics expose only environment variable names and redact known values from Podman output.

Error mapping keeps host/runtime failures as PrerequisiteError (exit 2), name/port/volume collisions as ConflictError (exit 6), missing containers/volumes as NotFoundError (exit 5), and invalid inputs as UsageError (exit 1).
inspect normalizes Podman JSON into a typed view with id, name, image, state, restart policy, labels, port bindings, named-volume mounts, and environment names (never values).

Volumes are created with io.easy-host.app=<app>; listing supports the label filter; create only adds --ignore when explicitly requested; removeContainer defaults to ignoreMissing for idempotent cleanup.
interfaces: containerName(app), volumeName(app, volume), publishSpec(bind, port, containerPort)
PODMAN_*_TIMEOUT_MS, DEFAULT_LOGS_TAIL, APP_LABEL, ROLE_LABEL, APP_ROLE_VALUE, IMAGE_LABEL, RESTART_POLICY, PODMAN_FAILURE_CODES
warnings: containerLogs defaults to follow=true and is still bounded by the 1h PODMAN_LOGS_TIMEOUT_MS to satisfy the finite-timeout rule.
The gated tests/integration/add.test.ts suite does not exist yet, so end-to-end Podman integration was not run.
No real Podman container or volume was created; all unit coverage uses the injected recording runner.
payload.taskDescription: Implement podman.ts with run, stop, remove, inspect, logs, and volume create/list/remove. Every call uses an argument array and a finite timeout. The run path sets --restart=always, names the container easy-host-<app>, publishes bind:port:containerPort, sets PORT, passes the merged environment without echoing it, mounts each declared named volume, and applies the io.easy-host labels. Tests use a recording runner to assert the exact argument arrays for a full run, a minimal run, a volume mount, and a log pass-through, and assert that env values never appear in diagnostics.
